summary: This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to reform the restaurant meals program by specifying that participating establishments must be retail food stores with prepared food sections, hot bars, or deli counters that are not primarily fast-food, and by requiring that eligible meals contain at least one fruit or vegetable and one protein.

scores.thoughts: This bill reforms the Restaurant Meals Program, which is part of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). By tightening eligibility for participating establishments and beneficiaries, it aims to reduce the scope and potentially the cost of the program, thus leading to less government spending.

The bill reforms the Restaurant Meals Program within SNAP by restricting eligible establishments, defining eligible meals, and excluding spouses of eligible individuals. These changes narrow the scope of who can receive benefits and where they can be used, thereby reducing the reach of this component of the social safety net.
